tasks.title: Per-side row-ordered rung table, ladder_pairs in tuple order, and the retired 'one table on both sides' prose
tasks.description: Replace services/option_ladder.py's single shared RUNG_OFFSETS dict (line 60) with the per-side, row-ordered tuple table of S-P24-1 -- {SIDE_CCS: ((1, 10), (2, 5), (3, 0), (4, -5)), SIDE_PCS: ((4, 5), (3, 0), (2, -5), (1, -10))} -- and make ladder_pairs read the side's tuple in tuple order (never sorted()), so PCS displays S3+5, S3, S3-5, S3-10 on rows 1-4 with the anchor (offset 0, label 3) on row 2 while CCS stays byte-identical. In the same edit retire the 'one offset table applied identically on both sides' invariant in the module docstring (line 7), the RUNG_OFFSETS comment (lines 59-60) and the ladder_pairs docstring (lines 112-119), and rewrite the SpreadRow docstring (line 85) to state that rung is the 1-based display row while the owner's labels are specification-only. Then re-baseline the five named ladder-suite cases; this is the phase's only production edit.
acceptance_criteria: Given services/option_ladder.py, When RUNG_OFFSETS is inspected, Then it is the single module-level offset table and equals {SIDE_CCS: ((1, 10), (2, 5), (3, 0), (4, -5)), SIDE_PCS: ((4, 5), (3, 0), (2, -5), (1, -10))} -- one entry per normalised side, each a 4-tuple of (logical label, short-strike offset from the anchor short strike) in display order top to bottom -- every offset is a whole multiple of STRIKE_STEP, the offset-0 entry is labelled 3 on both sides, SPREAD_WIDTH == 20 / STRIKE_STEP == 5 / SPREAD_WIDTH == 4 * STRIKE_STEP still hold, and neither RUNG_OFFSETS_PCS nor PCS_RUNG_OFFSETS occurs anywhere in services/, ui/, ibkr/, data/ or config/.

Given any anchor short strike A and either side, When ladder_pairs(A, side) is called, Then it returns exactly four (short, long) pairs in the side's tuple order -- CCS shorts A+10, A+5, A, A-5 and PCS shorts A+5, A, A-5, A-10 -- with each long exactly SPREAD_WIDTH away in the side's direction (short + 20 for CCS, short - 20 for PCS), the CCS output is identical to P23's for every anchor, ladder_pairs(7325, SIDE_PCS) is [(7330, 7310), (7325, 7305), (7320, 7300), (7315, 7295)] with the anchor pair on the second row (display row 2), ladder_pairs(7425)[2] is still (7425, 7445), and the signature ladder_pairs(anchor_short: float, side: str = SIDE_CCS) -> List[Tuple[float, float]], the _side_key normalisation and the ValueError for an unknown side are unchanged.

Given the ladder table's two readable facts, When the PCS row list is inspected, Then row order comes from tuple order and the label order from the label element independently: the PCS labels read [4, 3, 2, 1] top to bottom while the offsets read [5, 0, -5, -10] and the shorts descend, so a label-sorted iteration (which would yield labels 1, 2, 3, 4 = rows reversed) is observably different from the shipped sequence; CCS reads labels [1, 2, 3, 4] with offsets [10, 5, 0, -5].

Given the ladder module's prose, When it is read, Then the retired invariant is gone -- the module docstring bullet, the RUNG_OFFSETS comment and the ladder_pairs docstring state the per-side rule once with the row order and the anchor row per side (CCS anchor row 3, PCS anchor row 2) -- the string 'both sides' no longer occurs in services/option_ladder.py, and the ladder_pairs docstring names the canonical fixtures ladder_pairs(7425)[2] == (7425, 7445) and ladder_pairs(7325, SIDE_PCS)[1] == (7325, 7305) with the anchor on row 2.

Given the SpreadRow dataclass, When its docstring is read, Then it states that rung is the 1-based display row (the row's position top to bottom, 1..4, on both sides), that the owner's logical labels are specification data only and run 4, 3, 2, 1 against those positions on PCS (1, 2, 3, 4 on CCS), and that nothing renders a digit or a row-number column; the docstring contains both terms 'display row' and 'label'; and the field list, names, order and types are unchanged (rung, short, long, display_name, display_ask, display_bid, delta, gamma, matched) with rung still the first field.

Given tests/test_d65_option_ladder.py, When it is run, Then it is green and its five shared-table cases are re-baselined rather than weakened -- test_P23_T1_AC1_constants asserts the new per-side shape (keeping SPREAD_WIDTH == 4 * STRIKE_STEP and a whole-step check per side), test_P23_T1_AC1_four_pairs_per_side asserts the per-side offset lists (CCS [10, 5, 0, -5], PCS [5, 0, -5, -10]), test_P23_T1_AC1_one_offset_table_on_both_sides is replaced by a per-side test that keeps the two forbidden-name strings as the no-second-table guard and adds the anchor row per side, test_P23_T1_AC1_canonical_fixtures asserts CCS 7425/7445 and PCS 7330/7310, 7325/7305, 7320/7300, 7315/7295, and the PCS half of test_P23_T1_AC7_window_legs_eight_per_anchor uses anchor 7325 -- every other case in the suite passes unchanged, the module-is-Qt-free check still passes, the ladder suite's _fixture_guard legality examples (7340/7320) are left in place, and the wave result names each retired expectation.

Given every engine-suite case that reads a PCS row set -- window legs, kept and cancelled legs on a re-seat, chain-edge cases and the step direction -- When it runs, Then its expectations are re-derived against the per-side table and asserted exactly (four rows, exact strikes, _step_candidate('PCS', 7330) == 7335 because PCS still steps up by STRIKE_STEP), no case is weakened (no '>= 4' where exact rows were asserted, no deleted assertion), and the scored cases keep their exact credit figures.

Given tests/test_d66_delta_fence.py, When it is run, Then it pins the live modules' constants: DEFAULT_TARGET == 1.00, TARGET_MIN == 0.05, TARGET_MAX == 19.95, COLOUR_OFF and COLOUR_ON, MIN_ROWS == 4, SPREAD_WIDTH == 20 and STRIKE_STEP == 5.

Given the fence suite, When the eight rendered instrument names are checked, Then each matches AC-D66.1's regex verbatim ^SPX (Jan|Feb|Mar|Apr|May|Jun|Jul|Aug|Sep|Oct|Nov|Dec)(?:[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01]) \d+(?:\.\d+)?/\d+(?:\.\d+)?$ as rendered short-leg-first by format_instrument, and an ISO-dated name (SPX 2026-11-17 7330/7310) and a zero-padded-day name (SPX Nov07 7330/7310) are both rejected by the same regex.

Given the fence suite, When the rendered tables are inspected, Then each side shows four rows with the PCS anchor pair on row 2 and the CCS anchor pair on row 3, the table carries exactly the five columns HEADERS names (Financial instrument, ASK, BID, Delta, Gamma), and no row-number column or digit prefix exists in any instrument cell (Q117).

Given the fence suite, When the toggle and the Target are inspected, Then the toggle sits in the Target row to the right of the Target field and at the panel's content edge, its spread_state dynamic property reads 'on', then 'off' on OFF and 'on' again through ON -> OFF -> ON, the OFF colour is COLOUR_OFF and the ON colour COLOUR_ON, and the Target accepts 0.05 and 19.95 while rejecting 0.04 and 19.96 with one message and the last valid value retained (AC-D66.3 / AC-D66.4).

Given the fence suite, When the history record is checked, Then the marker prefix '[revises P23, 2026-11-18' is present at its five named sites in docs/requirements/requirements.md -- AC-D65.2, A187, A212, the P23 glossary's anchor entry and R142 -- asserted by site identifier rather than by raw occurrence count, and the retired phrases ('both sides', 'identically on both sides', 'same offset table on both sides') are absent from services/option_ladder.py (AC-D66.7).

Given the finished phase, When git diff --name-only db21672 is recorded, Then the listing is a subset of services/option_ladder.py + the five re-baselined suites (test_d65_option_ladder, test_d65_spread_engine, test_d65_option_stream, test_d65_option_panel, test_d65_residue) + tests/test_d66_delta_fence.py + docs/, and no production file outside services/option_ladder.py is listed (AC-D66.8).

Given the phase's suites, When they are run, Then the seven tests/test_d65_* suites plus the fence suite pass in one run, and the two banned typo pairs appear in no positive fixture, seed quote plan, probe record or canonical example, while the shipped negative guards that assert them absent (test_d65_residue.py's BANNED_EXAMPLES and its ban-list self-guard, the ladder suite's _fixture_guard docstring) still exist and still name them.
